title: Course Schedule IV
summary: Given a total of numCourses courses labeled from 0 to numCourses - 1, and an array of prerequisites indicating the order in which courses must be taken, determine for each query whether the first course in the query is a prerequisite for the second course.
statement: Given a total of numCourses courses labeled from 0 to numCourses - 1, and an array of prerequisites indicating the order in which courses must be taken, determine for each query whether the first course in the query is a prerequisite for the second course. Return a boolean array with the answers to these queries.
constraints: Each prerequisite edge before->after belongs to a directed acyclic graph.
For every query return whether the first course is a direct or indirect prerequisite of the second.
hints: Store direct prerequisite reachability in a boolean matrix.
For each possible middle course, connect every start that reaches it to every end it reaches.
Then answer each query by its matrix cell.
Floyd-Warshall induction proves that after each middle, paths using processed intermediate vertices are represented.
editorial: Floyd-Warshall induction proves that after each middle, paths using processed intermediate vertices are represented.

tests.explanation: Only course one reaches course zero.
The first two reachability queries are true; zero cannot reach one.
